title: Special Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development - April 16, 2025

items.title: Call to Order
notes: Chair C. James called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

items.title: Land Acknowledgement
notes: Chair C. James provided a land acknowledgement.

items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
notes: None declared.

items.title: Devin Sisak, EA, Barrier-free Cambridge
notes:
The delegate spoke on behalf of Barrier-free Cambridge and indicated support for service expansions. He spoke out against barriers to access and certain language used in the Mobility Plus application process, and highlighted the issues that can arise out of the language, which may be perceived as interrogatory and offensive, suggesting to instead include empowering language.

In reply to a question from the Committee, Doug Spooner, Acting Commissioner, Transportation Services, spoke to work being done for Mobility Plus, with more work being done to enhance service. Pertaining to the application, he indicated that an industry-standard form is used, which is affected by resources. D. Spooner also spoke to a policy review being done, to prevent misuse of the affordable transit program.

items.title: Lori (Heffner) Straus, Waterloo
notes: The delegate spoke in favour of transit services in the Region,  indicating that they found great improvements to buses over the years. The delegate brought suggestions forward for the Committee, asking them to consider improvements to internal bus arrangements, technology, and parking. The delegate further requested that more enhanced explanations be provided over the speaker at transfer points.

items.title: Michael Druker, Board Chair, Tri-Cities Transport Action Group (TriTAG)
notes:
The delegate spoke on behalf of Tri-Cities Transport Action Group, which encourages residents to use active transportation, including transit. The delegate favoured more growth in transit services and frequency of routes, citing the various costs associated with not enhancing transit programs, and spoke out against advertisements on buses.

In reply to a question from the Committee, the delegate clarified that ads that cover windows are the main concern as it pertains to branding.

items.title: Bruno Bustos Alegria, Waterloo
notes: The delegate spoke in favour of the GRT business plans, explaining that the transit system being financially accessible is a significant draw for people coming to Waterloo Region. The delegate indicated that more investments in GRT can lead to more accessibility and affordability in the area.

items.title: Brian Paul, Executive Director, Supportive Housing of Waterloo
notes:
The delegate provided a presentation, highlighting that not including seniors in the plan is a missed opportunity in the GRT business plan. The delegate spoke to the benefits of transit for older adults, as well as the benefits to the community for giving seniors affordable transit.

In reply to questions from the Committee, the delegate asserted that the Affordable Transit Program offered at the Region is insufficient in its current form for many seniors. He further indicated he is specifically in favour of more options for seniors in general.

items.title: Ellie Liu, Waterloo
notes: The delegate did not appear.

items.title: Raj Dosanjh, Stakeholder Relations Assistant and David Kuhn, Stakeholder Relations Officer, Waterloo Undergraduate Student Association
notes: The delegate spoke in favour of transit as a priority for students at the University of Waterloo and supported the general business plan, adding that the U-pass is a partnership worth protecting.

items.title: Matthew Harvey, Waterloo
notes:
The delegate spoke in favour of the GRT business plan, however, the Stage 2 ION was a notable omission from the plan. The delegate pointed to positives in the Regional transit systems as opposed to deficiencies in comparator municipalities, especially as it relates to frequency, which translates to dignified alternatives to car use.

In reply to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner spoke to the Stage 2 ION timeline which will look at service expansions.

items.title: Sam Goncalves-Horton, Waterloo
notes: The delegate spoke in favour of the GRT business plan, highlighting the need for frequency in terms of safety, equity, and inclusion.

items.title: Rajvir Sumal, Kitchener
notes:
The delegate spoke to a lack of transit coverage on South Huron road, and suggested a few options for the area which is missing services.

In reply to a question from the Committee, Kevan Marshall, Manager, Transit Development, spoke to improvements coming to Southwest Kitchener to improve coverage. He elaborated that part of balancing the frequent coverage network will be looking at service expansions as well.

Responding to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner spoke to challenges related to transit 'desert' zones, and indicated that the implementation plan was not included since staff avoid guessing service needs; however, he said that staff will look at goals to achieve service in areas that need improvement.

items.title: Barry Green, Cambridge
notes:
The delegate spoke to a need for transit improvements for Cambridge, pointing to extensive service available in Kitchener and Waterloo. The delegate pointed to issues around frequency that can affect work schedules.

In response to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner spoke to the process of how late-night trips are scheduled, and elaborated on items in the business plan that address concerns identified by B. Green. He indicated that the decisions for where and when routes are offered are data-driven.

items.title: Kevin den Dunnen, Kitchener
notes: The delegate spoke in support of the GRT business plan, especially as it relates to the frequent transit plan. The delegate added the Ken Sieling Museum should have better access.

items.title: Nathan Pineda, Kitchener
notes:
The delegate spoke in support of the GRT business plan, indicating the impact the plan would have on students. The delegate also discussed the issues that poor transit access can have on residents and referenced efficient transit systems in other countries. The delegate added that transit mitigates risks associated with motor vehicle accidents.

Replying to a question from the Committee, K. Marshall elaborated on the investments included in the plan that will assist in connecting newly developed areas to the downtown core.

items.title: Haadhi Faizal, Executive Director, More Transit Southern Ontario
notes:
The delegate spoke in favour of various aspects in the GRT business plan, and asked that the Committee support the plan. The delegate asked that the Committee consider fare capping, as well as open credit and debit payments. The delegate also spoke in favour of proof-of-payments systems, and that the Stage 2 ION was not discussed in the business plan, of which costs are a concern.

In reply to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner indicated that fare capping is being explored. Furthermore, he spoke to a new program on the GRT pay app which allows for credit and debit payments.

items.title: Abdullah Mir, Cambridge
notes:
The delegate spoke in favour of the GRT business plan, especially the frequent transit network, due to the opportunities and freedom greater frequency provides. The delegate supported the increase in routes and consistent schedules.

In reply to a question from the delegate, at the behest of Chair C. James, D. Spooner elaborated on the operating cost increases, and how increases in cost are being accounted for.

items.title: Swanny Graham, Kitchener
notes:
The delegate spoke to free ridership for seniors, pointing to other areas which have seen benefits to free transit for seniors. The delegate elaborated on certain areas which experience higher levels of senior ridership, especially in generally low ridership hours.

Replying to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner illustrated the 'flattened' ridership patterns over the last few years, and that data reveals smaller peaks throughout the day as opposed to historical patterns.

items.title: Madhav Garg, Waterloo
notes: The delegate spoke about crowding issues on certain routes, and urged that more work be done to increase the number of routes to mitigate these issues. The delegate also elaborated on long wait times and advocated for greater frequency for transit routes.

items.title: Ronak Patel, Kitchener
notes: The delegate did not appear.

items.title: Call for Delegations
notes:
Rick Chambers, Waterloo, spoke in relation to concerns noted from a train network committee they participate in, and spoke to seniors' passes benefits. The delegate elaborated that with increases in population, more work will be needed to be done and pointed to some positive work being done by GRT. The delegate cautioned against certain biases in transit which may result in inadequate attention for older adults.

Matthew Morgan, Waterloo, asked questions about the timeline for construction of the Kitchener Central Transit Hub (KCTH), the reintroduction of trolley buses, and the progress of Stage 2 ION. In reply to questions from the delegate, D. Spooner answered that KCTH should be operational by 2029-2030; he spoke to trolley buses being explored as a technology to be used in the Region; and lastly, he answered that the Stage 2 ION business plan is coming back in November, with ION stage 3 as a corridor identified in Official Plan, and only a planning piece at this point.
